title: Case: Grocery order marked delivered with a doorstep photo the customer disputes
context: A weekly grocery order from Umberlea Pantry, including chilled items, is marked delivered. The customer has been through the merchant's live chat and has now written to the desk.
initial_request: So to recap my evening. Tracker says delivered. Chat one tells me to ask the neighbours. Chat drops. Chat two wants my order number all over again. Chat drops because I dared to look at another tab. Chat three finally admits that is not my door, then tells me he can't do anything about it from chat, and the window closes on me. It is now gone seven. There is a week of food including chicken and the kids' yoghurts sat in a stranger's porch and I have nothing in for tomorrow's packed lunches. I am not knocking on a stranger's door in the dark to ask for my chicken back. Who actually sorts this out?

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Replacement authorisations to decide a replacement or refund for BP-6802, citing the photo reference and the chat agent's finding, and tell them what the customer has been through tonight.

must: Sends Replacement authorisations the order number BP-6802 and photo reference PH-2661-1 and asks for their decision on a replacement or refund.
States the evidence: the photo shows a door numbered 14 with a porch, the order address is 41 Tannery Walk, and the chat agent accepted the mismatch (CH-6117).

Tells them what she has already been through and what it leaves her with: about forty minutes and three dropped chat sessions for evidence that was there from the start, and a household with no food in for tomorrow, so they act tonight and contact her directly.
Says the carrier will not retrieve the order this evening, so recovery of the original is not an option to wait for.
must_not: Asks or suggests that Niamh go to number 14, or to any neighbour, to look for or collect the order.
Promises a replacement, a refund or a redelivery time.
Sends her back to live chat, or replies to her only that the matter is being looked into.
Says anything about whether the food would still be safe to eat if it were recovered.
Brings the substitution complaint, DL-1650, the billing statement or the locker notice into the message.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Order BP-6802 / DL-8451, weekly grocery order including chilled items, for Niamh Underhill at 41 Tannery Walk. The carrier marked it delivered at 17:38 today, left in porch, photo reference PH-2661-1. The photo shows a door numbered 14 with an enclosed porch. Her address is number 41 and has no porch. Your chat agent reviewed the photo and accepted that it does not match the order address (chat CH-6117), and noted that only your team can raise a replacement or refund. Nettlebank Arc Dispatch have told me the driver has finished and nobody can retrieve the order this evening. Please decide a replacement or refund for BP-6802 and contact her directly tonight if you can. It took her about forty minutes and three chat sessions that dropped on her to get the photo looked at, and she now has no food in for the household tomorrow, including the children's lunches. I have promised her nothing and have not asked her to go to the other property.
